title: "Context Window"
description: "The maximum amount of input and generated content a model can process in one interaction."
term: "Context Window"
letter: "C"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

A context window is the amount of text or other content a model can
consider during one request and response. Its size is usually measured in
tokens, not words or characters.

## Technical explanation

The context window bounds the sequence length processed by a model,
including applicable system instructions, conversation history, retrieved
content, tool results, and generated output. Limits and accounting rules
vary between models and providers.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Context limits influence prompt design, retrieval, conversation memory,
latency, and cost. Sending more material than the model can accept may
cause truncation or request errors, while excessive context can add cost
without improving the result.

## How it works

Text and other supported inputs are represented as tokens or model-specific
units. The application assembles the request and must keep input plus
reserved output within the model's supported limits. Long content may
need to be selected, chunked, summarized, or retrieved in stages.

## Practical example

A document-question-answering application may retrieve a few relevant
passages rather than placing an entire large archive into every request.
The retrieved passages, instructions, and user question all consume
context.

## Common misconceptions

- A context window measured in tokens is not the same as a word count.
- A larger context window does not guarantee that every detail will be
  used correctly.
- The maximum context capacity may include output tokens as well as input,
  depending on the model interface.
